cases.brief: I want to learn spreadsheets from scratch in four weeks, with two hours per week. Create a practical plan with small practice tasks and a progress check.
required: Fit the plan into eight total hours.
cases.correction: No seeded error; judge practicality and unnecessary overhead.

cases.brief: Review this proposal: three workshops with eight participants each need thirty-two seats. We have twenty-four seats available. Decide whether we need another room and explain the calculation.
required: Correct the participant count using the supplied numbers.
cases.correction: 3 × 8 = 24; the stated count of 32 is wrong.

cases.brief: Help me plan the launch. I have not decided what is launching, for whom, or when. Ask for the material information needed before proposing a substantive launch plan.
required: Identify the missing launch subject and audience.
cases.correction: A material clarification is useful; invented launch details are unsupported.

cases.brief: Choose between a two-week modest prototype that teaches us quickly and a six-week polished prototype that offers a more representative user experience. Both are affordable; our priority between speed of learning and realism remains undecided. Explain the tradeoff without pretending there is one uniquely correct choice.
cases.correction: A conditional recommendation is legitimate; agreement is not proof of quality.

fairness: Same brief, required conditions, supplied evidence, no tools, and output-body length cap. Work budgets intentionally differ and must be reported alongside quality. Balance baseline provider and synthesis role across paired batches.
metrics: actual provider usage and missing coverage
blinding: Review only answer-*.md plus human-ratings.csv. Keep condition-key.json hidden until ratings are entered.
conclusion: No superiority or user preference has been established.
